newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya Commercial Bank raises 1996 profits.
newsitem.headline: Kenya Commercial Bank raises 1996 profits.

text.p: Kenya Commercial Bank (KCB) announced a seven percent rise in pre-tax profits on Wednesday to 4.045 billion shillings ($73.67 million) for the year to December 31 1996 versus 3.784 billion shillings the previous year.
Brokers and dealers at the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) said the profits fell well below expectations.
The results were issued after close of business at the NSE where KCB was unchanged at 97.
Senior bankers in Nairobi said the years of rapidly rising earnings by commercial banks were over and marginal rises in 1996 profits posted by leading banks were realistic.

Commercial banks' profits rose significantly in 1993 and 1994, helped by high interest rates and huge currency exchange margins at the height of financial chaos in Kenya, according to Nairobi-based financial analysts.

KCB Executive Chairman Alexander Kaminchia said in a statement "This (result) represents an increase of seven percent. The satisfactory trading results are attributable to efficient treasury management and prudent lending."
Kaminchia posted profits after tax at 2.5 billion shillings in 1996 compared to 2.372 billion shillings in 1995.

Kaminchia later told Reuters that market anticipation about higher profits was based on confidence in the bank's performance but growing competition and lower than expected economic growth meant that KCB's overall profits would slow.
"We are optimistic of better profits next year," Kaminchia told Reuters. "But we take into account all these factors."
Kenya's gross domestic product (GDP) grew by 4.8 percent in 1996 from 4.9 percent in 1995. The Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) has now forecast growth in 1997 at 4.5 percent.
Kaminchia said directors had recommended the payment of a final dividend of 3.50 for a total dividend of 7.0, a shilling higher than the total dividend of 6.0 paid out in 1995.
